lines.en: Welcome! Dinner is almost ready. **Do you have any food allergies?**
lines.pt: Bem-vinda! O jantar está quase pronto. Você tem alguma alergia alimentar?
Tenho sim, sou alérgica a amendoim.

lines.en: Thanks for telling me. **Do you like** fish?
lines.pt: Obrigado por avisar. Você gosta de peixe?

lines.en: **I like** fish a lot. But **I don’t like** mushrooms.
lines.pt: Gosto muito de peixe. Mas não gosto de cogumelos.

lines.en: No mushrooms, then. **Do you prefer** rice or potatoes?
lines.pt: Sem cogumelos, então. Você prefere arroz ou batata?

lines.en: Perfect! Would you like some more salad?
**No, thank you. I’m full.** Everything was delicious.
lines.pt: Não, obrigada. Estou satisfeita. Estava tudo delicioso.

pages.title: Food Likes and Dislikes

unit.name: Eating out & shopping
map: Asking for the bill and paying

situation.text: A friend invites you to dinner at his home. He asks about your food. You say what you like, what you don’t like, what you prefer and that you have an allergy.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can talk about food: say what you like and don’t like, choose between two things, say an allergy and refuse politely.
canDo: Say: I like… / I don’t like…
Say an allergy: I’m allergic to…
Refuse politely: No, thank you. I’m full.
success: I say what I don’t like.
pages.think: Is there any food you really don’t like? How do you say no politely when someone offers it?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação: jantar na casa de um amigo.
solo: Pergunte o que o aluno não gosta de comer.
Leia o objetivo e os critérios.
group: Cada aluno diz uma comida que ama e uma que não gosta.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Food habits and allergies are important in the USA. Look at the cards and guess.

cards.note: Hosts often ask before cooking or serving. It is polite and important.
Many people are vegetarian or vegan, or avoid foods like gluten.
“No, thank you” plus a short reason is polite: “I’m full.”

qs.q: Why do hosts ask about allergies?
qs.pt: Por que o anfitrião pergunta sobre alergias?

levels.A1: Some food can make you sick.
levels.A2: A food allergy can be dangerous.
levels.B1: An allergy can be serious, so hosts ask before they cook.
levels.B2: Some allergic reactions are severe, which is why hosts and restaurants ask first.

qs.q: How do you say no to food politely?

levels.B1: No, thank you. It looks great, but I’m full.
levels.B2: That looks wonderful, but I’m afraid I couldn’t eat another bite.

qs.q: How do you say what you eat or don’t eat?
qs.pt: Como dizer o que você come ou não come?

levels.A2: I’m vegetarian. I don’t eat meat.
levels.B1: I’m vegetarian, so I don’t eat meat or fish.
levels.B2: I follow a vegetarian diet, but I do eat eggs and dairy.

pages.compare: In Brazil, hosts often insist on more food and say “come mais!”. In the USA, “no, thank you” is usually accepted at once. What happens where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto: alergias, dietas, recusa educada.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com o costume brasileiro de insistir.
answers: Q2: No, thank you. I’m full.
extra: Do you know someone with an allergy?
Is it rude to say no in your country?
stretch: B2: discuta dietas e convivência à mesa.

solo: 1ª escuta: quem está na cena? 2ª: alergia, gosta, não gosta, prefere, mais salada.
answers: Pass 2: peanuts · fish · mushrooms · rice · no (she is full).
extra: Is Nina polite? How do you know?

patterns.name: Preferences
patterns.formula: **I prefer** + A **(to / over)** B / **Do you prefer** A or B?
ex: Do you prefer rice or potatoes?

patterns.name: Polite refusal
ex: No, thank you. I don’t eat meat.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I do not care for mushrooms.
I have had enough, thank you.
register.note: “I don’t care for…” is polite and a little formal.

solo: Mostre os padrões no diálogo.
Troque as peças.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Short /ɪ/ and long /i/ change the word: chip /tʃɪp/ vs cheap /tʃip/. Short /ʊ/ and long /u/: full vs fool.

own.prompt: Write a sentence with “I’m full” and one with a food that has /ɪ/ or /i/ (fish, cheese, meat, chips).
own.criteria: Say them twice. Is the vowel short or long?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: vogais curtas × longas (chip/cheap, full/fool).
solo: Modele os pares e peça que identifique.
Aluno cria frases.
answers: Identify 1: I eat a chip. · Identify 2: I’m full.

pages.title: Group mission — dinner for everyone
pages.goal: Each group plans a dinner that every guest can eat, speaking only English.

missions.mission: Ask guests about allergies and likes. Decide a main dish everyone can eat.
missions.constraint: Use “Do you have any allergies?” once.

missions.mission: One guest is allergic to peanuts and one is vegetarian. Plan a menu.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m allergic to…” and “I don’t eat…”

missions.mission: Guests like different foods. Ask “Do you prefer…?” and choose a dessert together.

teach.goal: Realizar algo: planejar um jantar para todos.
answers: Modelo: “Do you have any allergies?” → “I’m allergic to peanuts.” → “No problem.”
extra: What if there is no dish for everyone?

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short reply to a friend’s dinner invitation: thank them, say your allergy and what you like.
pages.model: Hi Remy! Thanks for the invitation! **I’m allergic to** peanuts. **I like** fish and rice, but **I don’t like** mushrooms. See you on Friday!
checklist: I said what I like and don’t like.

solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: I like fish, but I don’t like mushrooms.
I’m allergic to peanuts, so I can’t eat that dish.
Would it be possible to make it without peanuts? I’m severely allergic.
I appreciate the offer, but I’d better avoid it for health reasons.
You’re most generous, though I’m afraid it’s not something I can take.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
